description.en: The micro FPV camera class with a 19 × 19 mm body, held in a frame bay or a printed cage by two side screws about which it tilts.
description.es: La clase de cámara FPV micro con cuerpo de 19 × 19 mm, sujeta en el hueco del marco o en una jaula impresa por dos tornillos laterales alrededor de los cuales se inclina.
description.fr: La classe de caméra FPV micro à corps de 19 × 19 mm, tenue dans la baie du châssis ou une cage imprimée par deux vis latérales autour desquelles elle s'incline.
description.pt: A classe de câmara FPV micro com corpo de 19 × 19 mm, presa no compartimento do quadro ou numa gaiola impressa por dois parafusos laterais em torno dos quais inclina.

governing.designation: Micro FPV camera, 19 × 19 mm body (COTS class)

frame_convention: Origin on the side-screw axis (the axis through the two side mounting screws, about which the camera tilts), midway between the two side faces. +x along the optical axis, out through the lens; +z up; +y to the camera's left. The side faces sit at y = ±9.5. The side faces sit at y = ±9.5 (half the cited 19 mm width); the front face (around the lens) at x = screw_axis_to_front_mm and the back face at x = screw_axis_to_front_mm − 20 (the cited 20 mm body length).

interfaces.note: Male: the body goes into the bay or cage. Symmetry 0: a mate's angle_deg sets the tilt about the side-screw axis.

Female: the camera's tapped side-screw hole, on the side-screw axis. Origin where that axis meets the side face (half the cited 19 mm body width from the mid-plane); the normal points out of the body. Symmetry 0: a mate's angle_deg is the tilt. Partners: the frame's camera_plate_* faces.

Female: the camera's tapped side-screw hole, on the side-screw axis. Origin where that axis meets the side face (half the cited 19 mm body width from the mid-plane); the normal points out of the body. Symmetry 0: a mate's angle_deg is the tilt. Partners: the frame's camera_plate_* faces.

Male: the body's front (lens-side) face seats on a flat receiving face (a printed cradle's floor). Origin at the face centre on the optical axis; the normal points out of the body. Symmetry 4: the 19 × 19 mm face is square. A cradle that the camera looks OUT through (a lens aperture in its floor) mates this face; the lens may stand proud of it.

Male: the body's back (cable-side) face seats on a flat receiving face (a printed cradle's floor). Origin at the face centre on the optical axis; the normal points out of the body. Symmetry 4: the 19 × 19 mm face is square. A cradle the camera looks AWAY from (lens out of the open side) mates this face.

review_status.note: Drafted in one pass by an agent (P4-STD lane, 2026-10-02); facts read from the cited sources on the access date; no language facet has had a native review.

notes: The side-screw thread and its height on the body are not published by the cited listings, so they are not facts here; the frame convention is defined by the screw axis instead of a number. The side, front and back faces are placed from the cited 19 mm width and 20 mm length alone; where the side screws sit along the body is a parameter (screw_axis_to_front_mm), not a fact.

label.es: Eje de tornillos laterales a la cara frontal
label.fr: Axe des vis latérales à la face avant
label.pt: Eixo dos parafusos laterais à face frontal

parameters.note: A convention, not a sourced fact: the cited listings give the 20 mm body length but not where the side screws sit along it. The default puts the axis mid-length. The back face is body_length − this behind the front. Set it from the chosen camera.
